original_run.note: Review applied to the original candidate output only; this public export was not reviewed.

role_scope.label: HR Generalist / People Operations
role_scope.title_boundary: Project label only; no claim that title strings are interchangeable or that market-wide equivalence is established.
role_scope.role_definition: A desk-research practice guide for US individual-contributor HR Generalist work; it is not a universal job description or qualification standard.

method_status.priority_order: authored learning sequence; not a measured importance, demand, or proficiency ranking

practice_sequence.title: Interpret policy and compliance boundaries
practice_sequence.rationale: Placed first because the occupational profile includes policy and rule-related work; the original author put this boundary before the other HR practice topics. This is a learning-order rationale, not a measured importance rank.
evidence_locators: O*NET OnLine 13-1071.00 › Knowledge › Law and Government
practice_sequence.evidence_strength: moderate; one occupational profile, no HR-Generalist-specific task-rating records, and no practitioner validation

practice_prompts.hiring_manager: Use a hypothetical policy scenario to check whether a candidate can find approved guidance, separate facts from interpretation, and describe a safe handoff; have qualified reviewers define any assessment.
practice_prompts.ic_hr_practitioner: Use an organization-approved source for a policy question, document the applicable rule and your role boundary, and identify the escalation route; do not use this guide as legal advice.
practice_prompts.job_seeker: Prepare an anonymized example that names the authoritative rule you consulted, how you explained it, and when you sought review.

practice_sequence.title: Listen carefully and use judgment in employee-relations work
practice_sequence.rationale: The occupational profile includes employee-relations work. The original author placed this after policy scope because sensitive employee situations call for careful intake and an appropriate next step; no relative-importance score is claimed.
evidence_locators: O*NET OnLine 13-1071.00 › Transferable Skills › Judgment and Decision Making
practice_sequence.evidence_strength: moderate; one occupational profile, no HR-Generalist-specific task-rating records, and no practitioner validation

practice_prompts.hiring_manager: If this work belongs in the role, define observable listening and escalation behaviors and use a consistent, job-related scenario reviewed by appropriate partners.
practice_prompts.ic_hr_practitioner: Rehearse a local intake process with a fictional scenario: clarify what happened, record only necessary facts, check confidentiality boundaries, and identify a referral or escalation step.
practice_prompts.job_seeker: Use a hypothetical or anonymized example to explain how you listened, checked assumptions, protected confidentiality, and knew when to escalate; do not disclose case details.

practice_sequence.title: Maintain accurate people records and HR documents
practice_sequence.rationale: The occupational profile includes employee-record and HR-document work. The original author placed this cross-cutting topic after employee-facing practice because it supports controlled transitions and reliable records; no software or proficiency level is inferred.
practice_sequence.evidence_strength: moderate; one occupational profile, no HR-Generalist-specific task-rating records, and no practitioner validation

practice_prompts.hiring_manager: Identify the records, documents, system access, retention rules, and decision authority local work requires before setting a selection exercise.
practice_prompts.ic_hr_practitioner: Walk through an approved document update: verify the source of truth, access permissions, version and approval controls, then check the resulting record without exposing employee data.
practice_prompts.job_seeker: Describe a non-confidential example of maintaining records, following version or privacy controls, and catching an error; name only tools the specific employer actually requires.

practice_sequence.title: Explain HR processes clearly to managers
practice_sequence.rationale: The occupational profile includes manager-facing information or training. The original author placed this after policy, employee-relations, and records practice as a communication application; posting counts were not used to rank it.
practice_sequence.evidence_strength: moderate; one occupational profile, no HR-Generalist-specific task-rating records, and no practitioner validation

practice_prompts.hiring_manager: If manager enablement is assigned locally, ask for a short explanation of a job-relevant process and evaluate accuracy, clarity, and escalation boundaries consistently.
practice_prompts.ic_hr_practitioner: Turn an approved process into a short manager briefing: state the next step, documentation needed, boundary of your authority, and escalation route; ask the manager to explain it back.
practice_prompts.job_seeker: Prepare a non-confidential example of making a process understandable, tailoring it to the audience, and clarifying what decision remained with the manager.

practice_sequence.title: Check people data and explain what it can support
practice_sequence.rationale: The occupational profile includes employment-data and reporting work. The original author placed this after policy, employee-facing, records, and manager-guidance practice as a separate analytic application; no tool, analytic depth, or prevalence is claimed.
evidence_locators: O*NET OnLine 13-1071.00 › Transferable Skills › Judgment and Decision Making
practice_sequence.evidence_strength: moderate; one occupational profile, no HR-Generalist-specific task-rating records, and no practitioner validation

practice_prompts.hiring_manager: Name the actual local reports and access boundaries, then use a consistent work sample only if local job analysis supports it.
practice_prompts.ic_hr_practitioner: Use a non-sensitive reporting example to verify the measure definition, denominator, time window, access rules, and limitations before sharing a finding.
practice_prompts.job_seeker: Explain a non-sensitive example of checking a data definition, comparing options, and communicating a finding with its limits; do not claim a tool is universally required.

limitations: One O*NET occupational profile anchors the retained sequence; it does not establish a complete HR-Generalist role analysis.
The admitted task-rating source is a dictionary, not HR-specific task-rating records; no numeric rating or proficiency is emitted.
The export makes no employer-demand, prevalence, trend, or universal experience-threshold claim.
No practitioner validation is claimed; the model review of the original is not validation and did not cover this export.
The seven employer-posting records are retained only as citation metadata, not public evidence claims.
